questions.stem: Which regulation section makes the STCW A-VIII/2 watchkeeping principles apply to Canadian vessels, and what two things does the master have to ensure?
options: MPR s. 320: the crew have enough rest and a deck watch is kept
Navigation Safety Regulations s. 137: a working language is chosen and recorded
MPR s. 213: the voyage is planned and a watch kept per A-VIII/2
MPR s. 171: the voyage is planned and the rating holds Bridge Watch Rating
questions.explanation: Section 213 of the MPR is the link to A-VIII/2 and names voyage planning and keeping a deck watch. Section 171 is the Bridge Watch Rating certificate, s. 320 is hours of rest and s. 137 of the Navigation Safety Regulations is the working language.

questions.stem: What is the first principle of watchkeeping on the bridge?
options: The bridge may be left unattended when at anchor
The bridge must never be left unattended
The bridge may be left unattended in daylight
The bridge may be left unattended if the autopilot is on
questions.explanation: The bridge must never be left unattended. Daylight, autopilot and being at anchor do not change that.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the factors the master weighs when deciding how many people are needed on watch?
options: The colour of the hull
The state of the navigation aids
Whether automatic steering is in use
Radio duties that take the officer's attention
questions.explanation: The listed factors are weather, visibility, daylight or darkness, closeness of navigational hazards, state of navigation aids, automatic steering, radio duties and unusual operational demands. Hull colour is not one of them.

questions.stem: A watch officer finishes a quick chart check and wants to go below for five minutes while a rating steers. What do the principles say?
options: The officer may go if the rating has at least 6 months of experience
The officer may go if the radar is on
The officer may go in daylight in open water
The officer must not leave the bridge until properly relieved
questions.explanation: In no circumstances may the officer leave the bridge until properly relieved. The rating's experience, radar and daylight do not alter that.

questions.stem: At 0300 the master walks onto the bridge and watches in silence from the chair. A vessel appears on the bow. Who is responsible for safe navigation?
options: The rating who saw it
Both equally, until the other vessel has passed clear
The OOW, until the master clearly takes over
The master, from the moment of arrival on the bridge
questions.explanation: The officer remains responsible until the master explicitly takes over responsibility and both understand it. Simply being present does not transfer it, and a rating never takes it over.

questions.stem: What does the principle on regular checks require of the officer of the watch?
options: Check the crew's hours of rest during each watch
Check course, position and speed regularly
Check engine temperatures
Check the passage plan only at the start of the watch
questions.explanation: The principle names course, position and speed, checked regularly against the planned route. Engine temperatures and rest hours are other jobs, and checking only once at the start is not "regular".

questions.stem: What is required of the officer of the watch regarding bridge equipment?
options: Know where all safety and nav kit is and how to use it
Knowledge of the radar only, since other equipment is optional
The ability to repair any equipment fault while underway
Knowledge of the manuals only, not where the kit is
questions.explanation: The officer must know where all the safety and navigational equipment is and how to operate it. Repair skills are not what the principle asks for.

questions.stem: The officer of the watch is on a quiet night watch and decides to do cargo paperwork at the chart table. Which principle does this conflict with?
options: The officer must leave the bridge at 0300 for a break
The officer must be relieved every hour at night
The officer must steer by hand at all times
No other duty may interfere with safe navigation
questions.explanation: The principles say the officer must not take on duties that interfere with safe navigation. Paperwork that takes attention from the watch is exactly that. The other options do not appear in the principles.

questions.stem: A vessel crosses open water in daylight with the autopilot on, a calm sea and good visibility. The master says the autopilot makes the watch factors irrelevant. What is the best answer?
options: He is right; check radar only
The master is wrong because automatic steering is never allowed in daylight
Autopilot is one factor; the others still decide
The master is right, so a watch is not needed with the autopilot on
questions.explanation: Automatic steering is one factor in the list, not a replacement for the watch. The bridge still must not be unattended and the officer still keeps the watch. Nothing in the principles bans autopilot use in daylight.

questions.stem: Which item does a relieving officer check at handover that links to the master's authority?
options: The ship's mooring plan for alongside
The master's standing orders
The galley menu for the week
The crew's shore leave list
questions.explanation: The relieving officer checks the master's standing orders along with position, course, speed, draught, weather, equipment and traffic.
